text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Voter registration gets off to a shaky start with confusion, walkouts and a poor turnout in many parts of the country.
- An American tourist Jesica Lundquist, 22, who went missing seven days ago in the Mount Kenya forest is found alive.
- Presidential hopeful Charity Ngilu calls on the Electoral Commission to advise the provincial administration against meddling with voter registration.
- Ten suspected hard-core criminals escape from a Nairobi police station after cutting the metal grill barring the windows.
- City hawkers defy a Nairobi City Council ultimatum to move out of the city centre streets.
- Police in Mombasa port detain the MV Ocean Explorer, which they suspect is carrying a haul of narcotic drugs.
- Eight men who claim to be the killers of Nairobi criminal lawyer Samuel Ndungi threaten to kill one of Ndungi's clients unless he pays them 150 million shillings.
- The Nairobi High Court orders the arrest of the City clerk for disobeying a court order.
